description: We are just beginners trying to learn
summary: MarsAtlas is a website that works like Google Maps, but for the planet Mars. It use real NASA and USGS data. You can zoom arond the whole planet, switch between many map layers, and search for places by name or coordinates. Click any spot to see its height, slope, rock type, and sunrise and sunst times. You can also plan a walking route, view real, nd see Mars in 3D. Planning a walk on Mars usually means using many separate tools, because the data is spread out. MarsAtlas puts it all in one place. Our route planner avoids steep ground and shows the walking time. It also gives a simple go/no-go checklist covering air suply, daylight, slope, radio contact, dust and cold. Every value shows its source, or says "No data" instead of guessing. astronauts will need to walk on Mars safely. A clear and honest map help teams make better decisions before they leave their base. It also let students and the public explore Mars for themselves. It runs in a web browser and even works offline, so anyone can use it.
details:
Working of our project

MarsAtlas is a website that work like Google Maps, but for Mars. It loads NASA Mars Trek map layers (176 of them, with 10 base maps) and USGS/IAU place names (2,052). You can pan, zoom nd search. Click any spot to se its height, slope, rock type, and sunrise and sunset times. Each value shows it source, or says "No data". Then you pick points on the map and the app plans a walking route that avoids steep ground. It shows the walking time and a go/no-go checklist for air supply, daylight, slope, radio contact, dust and cold. It also has a 3D globe, and a Mars clock.

benefits
All the data is in one place, so you don't need many tools. The safety checks are simple to read. It is free to use and works offline.

impact we want
We want future astronauts to plan Mars walk more safely. We also want students and the public to explore Mars themselve.

What tools did we use?
React, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind for the website. Leaflet for the flat map and Cesium for the 3D globe. Data from NASA Mars Trek, USGS and IAU. An AI assistant (Claude) helped us write the code.

How is it creative
It feels like Google Maps, so anyone can use it with no training. It also turns raw data into one clear answer: "Is this walk safe?" And it never guesses. If we don't have data, it says so.

we consider
Safety first. Honest data, with sources and clear notes on what is assumed. Easy use for beginners. Free open data. Working with a weak internet connection. We also list our limits: the elevation map is 200 m per pixel, so boulders do not show, and radiation data exists only at Gale crater.
